task.description: Design Letflow.EventStore.Registry for REQ-024 on branch feature/WF02-REQ024-20260816. Write lib/letflow/design/<module>.md per WF-02 Step 1's procedure. REWORK ITERATION 1: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAILed (handoffs/WF02-REQ024-20260816/step-01b-code-design-validator.json) on a BLOCKER: your existing draft's S4 interface note requires register_type/2, validate_payload/3, get_type/2 to accept prefix :: String.t() directly from the caller, citing Letflow.TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/2 as precedent -- but replay_migrations/2 actually takes tenant_id, not prefix (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex lines 153-181), internally resolving schema_name via Repo.get_by(Registration, tenant_id: tenant_id) and returning {:error, :tenant_not_provisioned} if unprovisioned. Fix your draft (lib/letflow/design/req024-event-type-registry.md) so it either (a) takes tenant_id and internally resolves schema_name via Letflow.TenantProvisioning (naming that as a real S6 cross-module dependency), matching replay_migrations/2's actual convention including a :tenant_not_provisioned-equivalent error case in all 3 function's error unions, or (b) keeps prefix :: String.t() but explicitly names the resolution mechanism the caller is expected to use before calling and the error case for an unprovisioned tenant. Read lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex directly yourself this time, don't re-cite from memory of your own prior draft.
acceptance_criteria: priv/repo/migrations gains an event_type_registry migration (schema-per-tenant per REQ-022) applying cleanly
register_type/2 rejects a second registration with the same (name, schema_version) with a distinct, testable error, not a generic changeset failure
validate_payload/2 against a payload missing a required field returns a failure result whose detail names the specific field_path (JSON Pointer form) and constraint, not just a boolean false
get_type/1 against an unregistered name returns an explicit :unknown_event_type-shaped error rather than nil or an exception
the moduledoc names the JSON Schema validation library choice as an explicit open question for CODE-DESIGNER, not a silently made decision

result.summary: Designed Letflow.EventStore.Registry (lib/letflow/event_store/registry.ex, first module in this new namespace -- REQ-023 has not merged, confirmed via git log main and handoffs/registry.json), its Ecto schema Letflow.EventStore.Registry.EventType (event_type_registry table, schema-per-tenant via REQ-022's :prefix mechanism, plain map()/jsonb json_schema column matching REQ-028's own jsonb-decodes-to-map precedent), a plain ValidationFailure struct, and a new pure Letflow.EventStore.Registry.JsonSchema validator module. Central decision (this design's centerpiece, per the requirement's own delegation): hand-roll a minimal JSON Schema validator matching R-Co's actual supported keyword subset (type, minimum/maximum, minLength/maxLength, enum, required, properties, items, additionalProperties:false-only -- verified directly against src/tools/json_schema.zig and spc-01's well-formedness table) rather than adding the ex_json_schema hex package. Reasoning: R-Co's own validator deliberately leaves $ref/allOf/anyOf/oneOf/pattern/format/patternProperties permissive/inert -- ex_json_schema would enforce those for real, a genuine behavioral divergence from the platform being ported, not a cosmetic gap; this mirrors 0002's own partial-library-adoption precedent and REQ-028's un-escalated hand-rolled-graph-validator precedent. No new mix.exs dependency (confirmed jason 1.4.5 already present, ex_json_schema absent from mix.lock) means this does not cross 0001/0002/0003's own bar for a new decision record -- none written; reasoning for why recorded explicitly in the design doc's own SS1.4 rather than silently assumed. Specified register_type/2 (stays literal arity per REQ-024's text, attrs+prefix), validate_payload/3 and get_type/2 (diverge to /3 and /2 respectively -- flagged explicitly and reasoned in SS4, since tenant-prefix threading is mandatory per AC1 and the requirement text never addressed how it threads through). validate_payload/3 returns validation failures alongside the error tuple ({:error, {:payload_validation_failed, failures}}) rather than porting a stateful last_validation_failures/1 accessor, matching the requirement's own suggested ownership-contract fix for Elixir's lack of Zig's slice-lifetime model. Added one Letflow-specific rule beyond R-Co (schema_version must exceed all existing versions for the name, not just avoid exact collision) with its own distinct :schema_version_not_monotonic error, called out explicitly as new rather than a straight port. Restated REQ-024's second open question (per-tenant vs global classification of event_type_registry) as instructed -- defaults to schema-per-tenant per Decision B's general rule, with corroborating-but-not-settling evidence recorded (0003 Dimension A groups this table with process_definitions as a 'regular CRUD table'; R-Co's own 002_event_type_registry.sql has no tenant_id column) -- flagged for REVIEWER re-confirmation, not presented as closed. Full acceptance-criteria traceability table included (SS8), explicitly addressing how AC5 is satisfied even though the library choice is now decided rather than left open. No implementation code -- signatures/type shapes, an Ecto field table, and one explicitly-labeled pseudocode algorithm sketch only.
